stays.name: Tokyo Dome Hotel
stays.blurb: This is an international hotel at competitive prices.

stays.name: Forest Hongo
stays.blurb: A bit nicer (and more expensive) than the standard business hotel, this is a good choice for visitors to Tokyo University, but not convenient otherwise.

stays.name: Toyoko Inn Korakuen Bunkyokuyakusho-mae
stays.blurb: Toyoko Inns are inexpensive business hotels, but have a good range of amenities.

stays.name: Mandarin Oriental
stays.blurb: This exclusive hotel has fabulous rooms, a world class spa and a Michelin 1 Star Signature Restaurant.

stays.name: Royal Park Hotel in Tokyo
stays.blurb: Five-star accommodation conveniently located in central Tokyo, ideal for business travelers and holiday makers.

stays.name: Tokyo Station Hotel
stays.blurb: If you ever wanted to sleep in a train station, then this might be the place to do it.

stays.name: Hotel Kizankan
stays.blurb: This basic business hotel is convenient for those visiting Tokyo University.

stays.name: Hotel Royal Oak Gotanda
stays.blurb: Less glamorous and a bit on the wrong side of the tracks, but cheap and accessible.

activities.title: Ramen counter crawl
activities.blurb: Order from a ticket machine, slurp loudly, repeat.

activities.title: Depachika food hall
activities.blurb: Department-store basements full of perfect snacks.

activities.title: Senso-ji at sunrise
activities.blurb: Tokyo's oldest temple before the crowds arrive.

activities.title: Digital art museum
activities.blurb: Walk-through rooms of light and projection.

activities.title: Golden Gai bar hop
activities.blurb: Tiny bars that seat six people each.

activities.title: Day hike at Mount Takao
activities.blurb: Forest trails an hour from the city, with a summit view.

activities.title: Shibuya Crossing and Sky
activities.blurb: Cross the world's busiest intersection, then see it from above.

activities.title: Kasai Rinkai Park
activities.blurb: The largest park in central Tokyo is just across the Edogawa River from Tokyo Disney Resort.

activities.title: Tsukiji outer market breakfast
activities.blurb: Tamagoyaki, tuna and oysters from street stalls.

activities.title: Sushi making class
activities.blurb: Learn to roll and shape nigiri, then eat your work.

activities.title: Meiji Shrine forest walk
activities.blurb: Giant torii gates and a calm forest in the city.

activities.title: Ghibli Museum
activities.blurb: Whimsical museum for Totoro fans. Tickets sell out fast.

activities.title: Izakaya night in Omoide Yokocho
activities.blurb: Yakitori smoke and tiny bars by the train tracks.

activities.title: Kamakura day trip
activities.blurb: Giant Buddha, temples and a beach town an hour away.

activities.title: Harajuku and Takeshita Street
activities.blurb: Wild fashion, crepes and people-watching.

activities.title: Tokyo Sea Life Park
activities.blurb: In the huge 2,200-ton tank, you can enjoy watching bluefin tuna darting swiftly around.

activities.title: Conveyor belt sushi
activities.blurb: Plates zip past, grab what looks good. Cheap and fun.

activities.title: Toyosu Market
activities.blurb: Toyosu is new home of the world's largest wholesale market for seafood and produce after its relocation from Tsukiji.

activities.title: Nogi's house and shrine
activities.blurb: General Nogi's house is a great example of Western architecture constructed during the Meiji period (19th century), mixing Japanese and Western elements.

activities.title: Tokyo Midtown
activities.blurb: Opened in April 2007, this competitor to Roppongi Hills boasts Tokyo's second tallest office building, a Ritz-Carlton and yet more endless acres of shopping and eating.

activities.title: Karaoke private room
activities.blurb: Rent a booth, order drinks, sing badly till late.

activities.title: Hakone and Mount Fuji views
activities.blurb: Lake cruise, ropeway and hot springs with Fuji on a clear day.

activities.title: Onsen evening at a sento
activities.blurb: Soak like a local in a neighborhood bathhouse.

activities.title: Tsukiji Outer Market
activities.blurb: For more than 80 years, Tsukiji was the world's largest wholesale fish market.

activities.title: Hama-rikyū Gardens
activities.blurb: It was built by 17th-century shoguns for their private enjoyment.

activities.title: Bunkyo Civic Center
activities.blurb: The lavish government building for the Bunkyo ward of Tokyo, once described in the Japan Times as "a colossal Pez candy dispenser." A free observation deck on the 25th floor, jutting out of the top like the Starship Ent…

activities.title: Hijiri-bashi Bridge
activities.blurb: On the Kanda river (神田川), on the border between Bunkyō and Chiyoda wards.

activities.title: Akihabara arcades
activities.blurb: Retro games, claw machines and anime shops.

activities.title: Koishikawa Kōrakuen
activities.blurb: Laid out in the 17th century, this splendid traditional garden boasts a large collection of trees and flowering plants that provide touches of beauty all year round.

activities.title: Shimokitazawa vintage hunt
activities.blurb: Thrift shops, record stores and little coffee bars.

activities.title: Kanda Yabu soba
activities.blurb: Yabu Soba opened its doors for business in 1880.

activities.title: Ninja Akasaka
activities.blurb: The entrance is a little difficult to find, but what do you expect from a restaurant designed like a hidden ninja fortress?

activities.title: The Tōyō Bunko
activities.blurb: The Toyo Bunko is a special library and a research institute of Oriental studies.

activities.title: Tokyo International Forum
activities.blurb: A massive, modern exhibition centre used for concerts, conventions and the like.
activities.address: located in front of Yurakuchō station

activities.title: Tokyo Dome City
activities.blurb: An attractions complex featuring a large indoor stadium, an amusement park, bowling alley, off-track betting center, and the LaQua shopping mall/spa (see Buy).

activities.title: Imperial Palace
activities.blurb: Surrounded by a series of moats and high walls, the site of the former Edo Castle has been the official residence of the Japanese imperial family since 1868.

activities.title: @home cafe
activities.blurb: This maid cafe has card games, drinks, food, and young women dressed up as maids to serve you.

activities.title: Ichiryu Bekkan
activities.blurb: Their speciality (and only dish) is the Seolleongtang soup, a white broth with beef, served with many side dishes including kimchi.

activities.title: RyuGin
activities.blurb: Moved from Roppongi in 2018. Combining a deep respect for the Japanese culinary heritage with a will to pushing boundaries has made Nihonryori RyuGin to regarded as one of the world's best restaurants.

activities.title: National Diet Building
activities.blurb: Housing Japan's bicameral legislature, it was built in the 1920s.

activities.title: Chidoriga-fuchi Moat
activities.blurb: One of, if not the most prominent cherry blossom site in Tokyo, and attracts throngs of people in its March-to-April peak season.
activities.address: on the northwest side of the Imperial gardens grounds

activities.title: Kabukiza Theater
activities.blurb: The best way to see traditional Japanese theater is to go to Kabuki-za for a single act, or hitomaku-mi, which lasts between one and two hours.
activities.address: 4-12-15 Ginza, near the corner of Showa-dori and Harumi-dori

activities.title: Kitanomaru Park
activities.blurb: Connected to the East Gardens on the north side is this park.

activities.title: Neko JaLaLa
activities.blurb: A 'cat cafe': you play with the shop's (very clean) cats while drinking tea.

activities.title: Benizuru
activities.blurb: Ludicrously fluffy pancakes served in wobbly stacks of three, with a selection of sweet and savoury toppings.

activities.title: Komagata Dozeu
activities.blurb: Another local institution, Komagata has been serving up loach hotpot (dojō nabe) for over 200 years.

activities.title: Yūshūkan War Memorial Museum
activities.blurb: An odd collection of military paraphernalia (including human torpedoes and letters from kamikaze pilots) and one-sided (allegedly revisionist according to the Chinese, Koreans and other Asian countries except Taiwan) de…

activities.title: Holy Resurrection Cathedral
activities.blurb: A beautifully-restored 1800s-vintage Russian Orthodox cathedral located near Ochanomizu Station on the Chuo Line.

activities.title: Hanayashiki
activities.blurb: The oldest amusement park in Japan.

activities.title: Kiyosumi Garden
activities.blurb: Not the most famous of Tokyo's gardens, but is quite lovely and uncrowded.

activities.title: Spa LaQua
activities.blurb: One of Tokyo's largest spa complexes, using water pumped from 1,700m below Tokyo.

activities.title: Tonkatsu Tōyama
activities.blurb: Classic tonkatsu pork cutlets deep-fried to perfection, with your choice of fatty rōsu or leaner hire.

activities.title: Sushizanmai
activities.blurb: The self-proclaimed "King Of Tuna", this is now a large chain but they originate from here in Tsukiji, where they have at least 7 locations and this three-story Honten.

activities.title: Tokyo National Museum of Modern Art
activities.blurb: With a modest permanent collection on display and regularly changing exhibitions, MOMAT is a nice place to kill a couple of hours after you've seen the Imperial Palace across the road.

activities.title: Fukagawa Edo Museum
activities.blurb: This intimate museum features a wonderfully recreated Tempo-period (1830-1843) neighbourhood - complete with homes, shops, narrow alleyways, and even the local rubbish dump.

activities.title: Pirates of Tokyo Bay
activities.blurb: Tokyo's long-running English and Japanese improv comedy group has performed unscripted shows at What the Dickens!
activities.address: What the Dickens!, Roob 6 Bldg 4F, 1-13-3 Ebisu-nishi, Shibuya-ku

activities.title: Diamond and Flower Ferris Wheel
activities.blurb: The park's most visible landmark is the Diamond and Flowers Ferris Wheel, so named due to its light shows that give it the appearance of a sparkling diamond or flower.

activities.title: Asakusa Naniwaya
activities.blurb: Asakusa Naniwaya branch the original of Taiyaki Naniwaya Sohonten (Azabu Jyu-ban).

activities.title: Tamahide
activities.blurb: In business since 1760, perhaps the oldest in Tokyo.

activities.title: Sushi Kanesaka
activities.blurb: The main branch of one of Japan's premier sushi restaurants with two Michelin stars, with another branch at the Palace Hotel, as well as two outposts in Singapore.

activities.title: Shibamata
activities.blurb: In Katsushika-ku, it features Taishakuten Temple (帝釈天) with its cozy shopping street that rivals Asakusa in liveliness while being much more authentic, lacking the overseas-tourist kitsch.

activities.title: Ship Lucky Dragon 5
activities.blurb: The restored fishing boat Lucky Dragon the crew of which became unfortunate victims of nuclear fallout fallowing a thermonuclear test at Bikini Atoll is on display at Tokyo Metropolitan Daigo Fukuryū Maru Exhibition Hal…

activities.title: Kamiya Bar
activities.blurb: The home of the Denki Bran cocktail, this was Japan's first Western-style bar when it first opened in 1880 and remains a truly local institution.

activities.title: Rikugien
activities.blurb: A classical Japanese park with ponds, hills and teahouses, that was built in 1695 by Yanagisawa Yoshiyasu, a Tokugawa daimyo.

activities.title: Cure Maid Cafe
activities.blurb: The original and not quite as over-the-top (or expensive) as some of the competition.

activities.title: Sushi Isshin
activities.blurb: This tiny 8-seater restaurant has had a Michelin star for 13 years running thanks to its uncompromisingly old-school Edo-style sushi, prepared with seasonal seafood and akasu red vinegar made from sake lees.

activities.title: Ramen Cooking Tokyo
activities.blurb: English-only small-group cooking class (maximum 8 participants) where visitors prepare ramen and sushi in a 3-hour session, with a sake pairing of three varieties.

activities.title: St. Mary's Cathedral
activities.blurb: Seat of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Tokyo.

activities.title: Tokyo Big Sight
activities.blurb: If you're visiting Tokyo on business, this, Japan's largest exhibition and convention center, might already be your destination.

activities.title: AKB48 theater
activities.blurb: AKB48 is a home-grown, all-girl idol group — their name comes from Akihabara — which started in 2005 and quickly became the best-selling female group in Japan.
